newsitem.title: FRANCE: SGS-Thomson drops on profit warning.
newsitem.headline: SGS-Thomson drops on profit warning.

text.p: Shares in semiconductor group SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV fell sharply on Friday after the company issued a profit warning.
At 0819 GMT, SGS-Thomson shares were down 6.58 percent at 440 francs.
SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV said overnight its second-quarter profit was likely to be within a range approximating first-quarter earnings of $0.65 per share.
That compares with an analysts' consensus forecast of $0.85 per share, according to First Call.
The company also said it expected second-quarter revenues to fall short of analysts' expectations, based on the results of the first two months of the quarter.
It said its gross margin would show little change from the first quarter because of a short-term shift in product mix.
In the first two months of the quarter, a larger-than-expected percentage of sales were derived from commodity products, the Franco-Italian semiconductor maker said.

Worldwide demand for those products has strengthened in the last several months, but pricing remains low and the gross margin associated with them is much less than that of SGS-Thomson's differentiated products, it said in a statement released in New York.

Looking ahead, SGS-Thomson said it still expected to show progressive improvement in 1997. It said second-half results should benefit from better overall market conditions and a stronger contribiution from sales of differentiated products.

It said the third-quarter order backlog as of May 31 was "substantially above second-quarter levels and reflects a significant increase in order visibility over the first and second quarters of 1997."
